nodes.name: Stop the pump and start the standby unit to prevent further damage
Plan a controlled shutdown and switch to the standby pump
Throttle the discharge valve to return flow to the Preferred Operating Region (70-120 m3/h)
Temporarily reduce flow (throttle discharge) to cut suction-side losses until the cause is removed
Open the discharge valve / restore the discharge path; verify minimum-flow bypass is open
Restore suction supply (tank level, suction valve) and re-prime before restart
Recalculate NPSHa vs. NPSH3 at the actual flow and fluid temperature
Take an FFT vibration spectrum (1x, 2x, bearing defect frequencies) to confirm the mechanical fault
Run a performance test and compare measured H-Q points with the OEM curve
Check bearing lubricant level, condition and contamination (oil analysis)
Check supply voltage balance, motor insulation resistance and overload relay settings
Clean or replace the suction strainer element
Restore suction tank level; check level control and make-up supply
Restore fluid cooling (check upstream cooler) to lower the vapour pressure
Fully open the suction isolation valve (never throttle on the suction side)
Vent the casing and re-prime; locate and seal air-ingress points
Laser-align pump and motor shafts to coupling tolerance
Check pipe supports and remove nozzle loads (pipe strain)
Check and correct soft foot, grout and anchor bolts
Replenish or replace the lubricant with the specified grade
Replace the drive-end bearing; inspect shaft and housing fits
Clean and dynamically balance the impeller (ISO 21940-11 grade G6.3)
Inspect and repair or replace the impeller
Replace wear rings to restore the design running clearance
Replace seal faces and elastomers; verify the seal flush plan
Inspect and repair the discharge check valve
Inspect and clear the discharge line / downstream blockage
With the pump isolated, check the rotor turns freely; inspect for rubbing
Verify fluid density and viscosity against the pump datasheet
Cavitation
nodes.description: Vapour bubbles form at the impeller eye and collapse inside the impeller.
nodes.physics: When the absolute pressure at the impeller eye approaches the fluid's vapour pressure (NPSHa approaching NPSH3), vapour bubbles form and then collapse violently in higher-pressure regions. The implosions cause broadband vibration and noise, pit the vanes, and vapour blocking the passages breaks down the developed head and flow.

nodes.name: Drive-end bearing degradation
nodes.description: Rolling-element bearing distress (lubrication failure, contamination or fatigue).
nodes.physics: Loss of the lubricant film, contamination or fatigue spalling increases rolling friction, raising bearing temperature; defects on races or rolling elements generate impacts that raise radial vibration. Higher temperature degrades the lubricant further, a self-accelerating loop.

nodes.name: Pump-motor shaft misalignment
nodes.description: Angular or parallel offset between pump and motor shafts.
nodes.physics: The coupling is forced to flex every revolution, producing cyclic reaction forces that are characteristically strong in the axial direction (1x and 2x running speed) and add load to the bearings, which raises bearing temperature.

nodes.name: Rotor / impeller imbalance
nodes.description: Mass centre of the rotor offset from its axis of rotation.
nodes.physics: The offset mass creates a centrifugal force F = m*e*omega^2 rotating at 1x running speed, giving predominantly radial vibration. Hydraulic performance (head, NPSH) is unaffected, which distinguishes imbalance from cavitation: while the NPSH margin is low, vibration cannot be attributed to imbalance.

nodes.name: Mechanical seal leakage
nodes.description: Process fluid escaping across the mechanical seal faces.
nodes.physics: The seal relies on a thin fluid film between rotating and stationary faces. Face wear, thermal distortion or heat-checking (e.g. after dry running) and elastomer degradation open the gap; leakage trips the leak detector and frictional heat raises the seal-chamber temperature.

nodes.name: Dry running (loss of suction)
nodes.description: The pump runs without liquid in the casing.
nodes.physics: Without liquid the impeller cannot develop head: discharge pressure collapses toward suction pressure and the head ratio falls to near zero. The motor only supplies mechanical losses, so current drops well below normal. The seal faces lose their lubricating and cooling film and overheat within minutes.

nodes.name: Deadheading (blocked discharge)
nodes.description: The pump runs against a closed or blocked discharge.
nodes.physics: The pump operates at shut-off: pressure rises to the shut-off head while flow is ~zero. For a radial centrifugal pump absorbed power is minimum at shut-off, so motor current FALLS (it does not rise). All absorbed power heats the trapped liquid, so seal-chamber temperature climbs and the liquid can eventually flash to vapour.

nodes.name: Hydraulic degradation (impeller / wear-ring wear)
nodes.description: Pump develops less head than its OEM curve at the same flow.
nodes.physics: Vane erosion and opened wear-ring clearances increase internal recirculation from discharge back to suction, so the pump develops less head than its curve at the measured flow (head ratio < 1). NPSH margin stays healthy and the motor stays loaded, which separates wear from cavitation and from loss of suction.

nodes.name: Motor overload
nodes.description: Motor draws more than its full-load current.
nodes.physics: Motor current tracks shaft load. For a radial centrifugal pump absorbed power rises with flow, so running far right on the curve (runout) overloads the motor; mechanical drag, a denser fluid or a low/unbalanced supply voltage do the same. The extra I^2R losses raise the winding temperature toward the insulation limit.

Clogged suction strainer
nodes.description: Debris on the strainer adds suction-side pressure loss, lowering NPSHa.

nodes.name: Low suction tank level
nodes.description: Reduced static head (and possible vortexing) lowers NPSHa.

nodes.name: High fluid temperature
nodes.description: Vapour pressure rises steeply with temperature, consuming the NPSH margin.

nodes.name: Partially closed suction valve
nodes.description: A throttled suction valve adds pressure loss after the strainer. Confirmed by elimination: low suction pressure with normal strainer DP, tank level and fluid temperature.

nodes.name: Runout operation (low system resistance)
nodes.description: Flow far beyond rated raises NPSH3, suction losses and absorbed power.

nodes.name: Empty suction tank
nodes.description: No liquid reaches the pump suction.

nodes.name: Closed suction valve
nodes.description: Suction isolation valve left closed; pump pulls a vacuum on its own casing.

nodes.name: Air ingress / loss of prime
nodes.description: Air leaking into the suction line or casing displaces the liquid.

nodes.name: Insufficient or degraded lubrication
nodes.description: Low oil level, wrong grade or oxidised lubricant.

nodes.name: Lubricant contamination
nodes.description: Water or particles in the lubricant damage raceways.

nodes.name: Bearing fatigue (end of L10 life)
nodes.description: Sub-surface fatigue spalling after the rated number of cycles.

nodes.name: Improper alignment after installation / overhaul
nodes.description: Shafts not aligned to tolerance when the pump was last installed.

nodes.name: Pipe strain on pump nozzles
nodes.description: Piping forces distort the casing and move the pump shaft.

nodes.name: Soft foot / foundation settlement
nodes.description: Uneven support lets the machine move when bolts are tightened or under load.

nodes.name: Uneven impeller fouling
nodes.description: Non-uniform deposits shift the impeller's mass centre.

nodes.name: Impeller damage (foreign object / broken vane)
nodes.description: Missing or damaged vane material unbalances the rotor and reduces head.

nodes.name: Excessive wear-ring clearance
nodes.description: Abrasive wear opens the running clearance and increases internal recirculation.

nodes.name: Seal face wear (end of life)
nodes.description: Normal wear of the carbon / silicon-carbide faces.

nodes.name: Seal elastomer degradation
nodes.description: O-rings harden or swell from temperature or chemical attack.

nodes.name: Closed discharge valve
nodes.description: Discharge isolation valve closed or not opened after start-up.

nodes.name: Check valve stuck closed
nodes.description: The non-return valve disc is jammed shut.

nodes.name: Downstream line blockage
nodes.description: Debris or a closed valve further downstream blocks the discharge line.

nodes.name: Mechanical binding / rubbing
nodes.description: Rotor rubbing on stationary parts adds friction load.

nodes.name: Low or unbalanced supply voltage
nodes.description: For the same load, lower or unbalanced voltage increases motor current.

nodes.name: Fluid denser or more viscous than design
nodes.description: Absorbed power is proportional to density (and rises with viscosity).
